812:
(a) The developer is required to obtain approval of any outside regulatory agencies as required for the project. The developer shall notify the city before submittal to any outside regulatory agency. Upon approval from an outside regulatory agency the developer shall submit an original copy of the approved plans to the city. No permit shall be issued until copies of outside agency approvals have been received.
(b) Approval of a plan set by an outside regulatory agency does not constitute approval of a plan by the city. When a plan set requires modifications by the city extensive enough to warrant resubmittal the developer shall resubmit to that outside regulatory agency and obtain approval for the modifications. Examples of outside regulatory agencies include, but are not limited to, state soil and water conservation (NRCS), state environmental protection division (GAEPD water and sewer) fire marshal, state department of transportation, etc.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.2, 4-24-2017)
813:
When a developer is prepared to submit plans for review to the city, a submittal package must be composed. A submittal package consists of, but is not limited to:
(1) Plan application. Applications for the varying plans may be obtained from the city. The developer shall complete the application in its entirety.
(2) Plan review fees. Fees should be submitted as outlined in the city fee schedule. If payment for the fees is not submitted at this time the city should not accept the plans nor should a review of the plans be made. Should the fees submitted not be sufficient to cover the cost, the city should not provide review comments or approval until such time as fees have been submitted.
(3) Permit application. Applications for the varying permits may be obtained from the city. The developer shall complete the application in its entirety.
(4) Plan sets. The developer shall submit a sufficient number of plans as dictated by the city. The number of plans required will be dependent on the type of plan submitted. A .pdf version of each plan submitted must be provided on CD.
(5) Outside agency approval. Any outside regulatory agency approval should be presented with the submittal package. No permit shall be issued without original copies of all outside regulatory agency approvals submitted to the city.
(6) Waivers. Any waivers required should be included for review by the city.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.3, 4-24-2017)
814:
If the developer wishes to vary any of the requirements of the development regulations as a part of the plan approval procedure, those requested changes shall be set forth on a form as provided by the city. The city manager shall be authorized to grant waivers to the provisions of the development regulations. However, if a waiver is not specifically approved by the city manager, it shall not be considered to have been granted. For example, approval of the site plan shall not constitute approval of waivers depicted graphically but not approved by the city manager. The city manager may utilize the assistance of outside experts in the specific field of the requested waiver to assist with the decision. At the discretion of the city manager, a decision on a waiver may be placed on the city council agenda for a decision. A waiver is not transferable from one plan set to the next, excluding revisions to plan sets, even if a waiver was previously granted for the same tract of land, parcel, area or development. Each plan set, excluding revisions to plan sets, must establish the justification for a waiver. The application fee for a waiver will be as shown on the approved fee schedule as set by the mayor and council.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.4, 4-24-2017)
815:
The city may utilize any resources deemed necessary to review plans to ensure conformance with this chapter. Unless required under law the time required to review plans shall be as deemed necessary by the city.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.5, 4-24-2017)
816:
The city utilizes outside contractors to perform plan reviews for most types of plan sets. Plan review fees will be based upon the actual cost of plan reviews plus administrative costs associated with each review. The city maintains a fee schedule with average costs of plan review fees which are due at time of submittal. Actual costs may vary and any amount due will be required to be paid before any permits, approvals, etc., will be issued.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.6, 4-24-2017)
817:
(a) Approved plans shall be valid for a period not to exceed 12 months from the date of approval unless an extension in writing is granted.
(b) Approval of construction plans shall expire 12 months from the date of approval without the issuance of a building permit from the city.
(c) If a discrepancy occurs between the approved plans and the city's development standards, unless a waiver has been obtained, the development standards shall be the superseding document.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.7, 4-24-2017)
818:
Any changes from the approved plans will require that the engineer submit revised drawings along with a request explaining the reason for the change prior to construction of the change. Any deviation from city standards will be considered a major change as will any change that will affect capacity, longevity, operation or maintenance of the facility. Any deviation from approved materials will not be accepted without prior approval.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.8, 4-24-2017)
819:
The developer is required to schedule a meeting with the city and all public and/or private utilities for the purpose of discussing the construction and inspection of the proposed development. The pre-construction conference is required before the issuance of any permits unless waived by all affected city departments.
(1) Schedule a pre-construction meeting with the city manager or his representative and other city and regulatory agency representatives prior to start of any construction. The contractor's superintendent shall attend the meeting. The date and time of the meeting shall be as scheduled by the city manager. Such pre-construction meeting shall not relieve the contractor from cooperating should the city or other regulatory agencies desire additional meetings or visits.
(2) Submit a proposed construction schedule to the city at the pre-construction meeting.
(3) Perform work in a sequence to be agreed to at the pre-construction meeting, unless otherwise directed.
(4) Coordinate with related construction projects of the city or by others, if any.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.9, 4-24-2017)
820:
(a) Prior to the issuance of any permit which includes the construction or installation of infrastructure to be dedicated to the city within rights-of-way, easements, or other property either owned by, to be dedicated, conveyed, or used by the city said contractor, property owner, or entity working on said property for himself and for all subcontractors must provide the city a liability insurance certificate of $1,000,000.00 in general liability insurance listing the city as a co-insured or indicating that coverage under said policy is provided for the city.
(b) Said certificate shall be presented to the city manager prior to the issuance of any construction related permits, and must be approved by him prior to the issuance of any construction related permits.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.10, 4-24-2017)
821:
The city shall require the submittal of a performance bond or irrevocable letter of credit prior to issuance of a permit in order to ensure that the infrastructure is installed by the developer or his contractor as required by the approved plan. The performance security shall contain forfeiture provisions for failure to function and perform as intended and for failure to complete such work as specified in the approved plan. The amount of the installation performance security shall be for 125 percent of the total estimated construction cost. Construction costs shall be determined by cost tabulation sheets provided by the developer. The city reserves the right to verify the costs provided through utilization of outside sources.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.11, 4-24-2017)
822:
(a) No construction shall be allowed until a construction permit has been issued by the city. The contractor shall submit one copy of the approved construction plans which have been stamped approved. The contractor shall furnish his name, address, and telephone number. He shall also furnish the name of the person in charge of the project and any subcontractors and the name and telephone number of a responsible person who can be contacted in case of emergencies during nonworking hours.
(b) The contractor shall notify the city 24 hours prior to doing any work. Once the contractor begins work, he shall proceed in a workmanlike manner and shall complete the work in a reasonable time without undue off days and periods of inactivity which make it hard for the city to keep up with his activity.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.12, 4-24-2017)
823:
Developers and contractors shall limit work to the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. The city may allow work outside of these hours on a case-by-case basis. Should the developer desire to work outside of these hours, a request should be submitted in writing to the city manager. If the request is approved, a written approval will be provided and must be displayed within the permit board.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 103.13, 4-24-2017)
826:
(a) Contractors are solely and fully responsible for the protection and safety of the site of the work, including the public, the workmen, the city's employees and representatives, and other regulatory personnel.
(b) Contractors shall provide all construction aids and equipment required for job safety, for protection of the public, to facilitate execution of the work and to facilitate access by the city representatives and regulatory personnel.
(c) Contractors shall provide fences, barriers, lights, signs, ladders, sheeting, shoring, railings, hoists, and other such facilities and equipment and maintain all such facilities and equipment in like new condition.
(d) Contractors shall comply with traffic control and safety requirements of local authorities and any state DOT permits applicable to the work.
(e) Contractors shall provide and operate traffic control and directional signals, barricades, warning signs, etc., to direct and maintain an orderly safe flow of traffic in all areas affected by the contractor's operations.
(f) All traffic control signs, barricades, etc., shall be clean, in a like new condition, and easily seen and read. Old, faded, and/or dirty signs will not be allowed at the site and shall be replaced.
(g) Contractors shall provide qualified and suitably equipped flaggers whenever and wherever construction operations encroach on traffic lanes, as required for regulation of traffic, and/or as required by applicable DOT permits, and/or the city representatives.
(h) Contractors shall provide lights at night and during periods of low visibility to clearly delineate traffic lanes and to alert traffic to construction operations underway.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 104.1, 4-24-2017)
827:
(a) Access to the existing facilities and private property shall be maintained at all times; provide crushed stone, cover plates, or temporary pavement as necessary to maintain roadways in a safe and passable condition at all times until the permanent roadway surface is repaired.
(b) All existing benchmarks, monuments, and other reference points shall be carefully protected. Replacement, if required, shall be by a licensed land surveyor at the contractor's cost.
(c) All work required on public rights-of-way will be conducted in strict conformance with rules, regulations, and permit conditions of governing bodies having jurisdiction.
(d) If articles of historical or archaeological value, including coins, fossils, and articles of antiquity are uncovered, all construction activities in the vicinity shall be stopped and the city shall be notified immediately. All such articles of historical or archaeological value found in the public rights-of-way shall remain the property of the city.
(e) Blasting operations for rock removal shall not be conducted within six feet of the edge of any public roadway pavement. All blasting operations will require approval of the city.
(f) Existing grades on the site must be checked prior to starting. Beginning of any grading shall constitute acceptance of the existing site conditions.
(g) Prior to starting any excavation, the Utilities Protection Center "Call Before You Dig" must be contacted; telephone number is 811.
(h) Allowable borrow or waste areas, unless designated on the drawings, shall be approved by the city prior to start of construction.
(i) All unsuitable excavated material must be properly disposed of in a manner acceptable to the city and in a manner that will not adversely impact the environment.
(j) The bypassing of raw wastewater onto the ground or into a receiving stream is prohibited.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 104.2, 4-24-2017)
828:
The following must be provided:
(1) Temporary electric power service to the site for the duration of construction activities as required.
(2) Temporary lighting for the site as necessary for safety, for construction operations, and for the contractor's and city's quality control inspections.
(3) Temporary telephone service to the site. The contractor's personnel shall have a functional cell telephone activated at the site at all times that construction activities are taking place.
(4) Trash containers for the site to properly dispose of all trash, debris and garbage as necessary to keep the site clean and sanitary at all times, including storage and parking area, along access roads, and haul routes.
(5) Temporary water as needed for construction activities on the site.
(6) Required toilet facilities and enclosures and maintained in clean and sanitary condition for workmen's use.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 104.3, 4-24-2017)
829:
The following environmental controls are required:
(1) Compliance with all local, state, and federal (OSHA) noise control requirements. Limit all operations, except during emergencies, to daylight periods when noise from operations will not disturb residential neighborhoods.
(2) Positive dust control methods at the site and all off-site borrow areas. Apply water or other dust control materials as required to minimize dust emissions from construction operations, and provide positive means to prevent air-borne dust from dispersing into the atmosphere at all times. Prevent dust being a nuisance to the public, the neighbors, and a detriment to the performance of work at the site.
(3) Methods to control surface water to prevent damage to the stored materials, installed work, the site, and adjoining properties. Control all earthwork filling, grading and ditching to direct surface drainage away from excavations, pits, tunnels and other construction areas; and to direct drainage to proper runoff.
(4) Maintenance of the site and all areas under the contractor's control free of extraneous debris and prevent accumulation of debris at construction site, storage and parking areas, or along access roads.
(5) Methods, means and facilities required to prevent contamination of soil, water or atmosphere by the discharge or spills of noxious substances from construction operations. Take special measures to prevent harmful substances from entering public waters. Prevent disposal of wastes, effluent, chemicals, or other such substances adjacent to streams, or in sanitary or storm sewers.
(6) No clearing or grading operations are to begin until a land disturbance permit has been issued. Periodically inspect excavated or disturbed areas to detect any evidence of the start of erosion, apply corrective measures as required to control erosion. Provide supplementary erosion and runoff control measures when it becomes apparent that additional problems exist.
(7) Removal of all temporary facilities and controls from the site promptly upon completion of the work.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 104.4, 4-24-2017)
830:
Authorized representatives of the city, which may include city employees, the city engineer or his representative, state or federal agencies, shall have access to the site for inspection at any time.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 104.5, 4-24-2017)
831:
(a) The developer's contractor will be responsible for the quality, accuracy and workmanship of his completed work.
(b) City personnel will visit the job site on a periodic basis and will make spot checks as they deem appropriate. The city shall have the right to review and inspect all construction and may reject any work that does not meet quality control standards. The city maintains the right to refuse performing inspections at unsafe worksites.
(c) The city inspector may direct that the contractor notify the city and receive inspection approval prior to concealing certain work such as manhole foundations, pipe bedding, tees, bends, service laterals, or other appurtenances. At the city's discretion, the city may require work to be uncovered which was not inspected prior to backfilling.
(d) Cost for all inspections and testing shall be paid for by the developer.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 104.6, 4-24-2017)
832:
The city reserves the right to require further testing or more stringent inspections for any reason to ensure quality workmanship and materials.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 104.7, 4-24-2017)
835:
(a) The contractor shall request in writing a final inspection. This final inspection will generally include spot checks and a complete overview of the project.
(b) After any discrepancies are corrected and all other requirements of this chapter are satisfied, the city will issue a letter certifying conditional acceptance of any infrastructure intended to be dedicated to the city for non-subdivision developments. This letter shall commence the start of the 18-month warranty period which is required of the contractor. On projects having phased development, this letter will allow the developer to apply for a permit for the next phase of development.
(c) For subdivision developments the acceptance by the city council of the final plat shall begin the warranty period.
(d) The performance bond or letter of credit will be released by the city upon conditional acceptance.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 105.1, 4-24-2017)
836:
(a) The developer shall maintain the improvements in his development for a period of 18 months from the date the city issues approval of the final plat for subdivisions or a conditional acceptance letter for non-subdivision developments. At the end of the 18-month maintenance period, the city shall perform an inspection of the development and all improvements. The developer shall be notified by the city of the inspection results in writing within 30 days from the date of the inspection. The maintenance bond shall be released upon the issuance of a letter stating approval of the development by the city. (The final plat shall note said maintenance period and note the date that street dedication to the city shall occur.)
(b) If repairs are needed at the end of the 18-month maintenance period in order for the improvements to meet city specifications, the developer shall be required to make such repairs within 60 days, after written notification by the city. If the repairs are not completed within said time, and the developer fails to show a legitimate hardship, as determined by the city, which inhibits the completion of the repairs, the maintenance bond shall be called in to pay for the repairs. Should the amount of the maintenance bond be inadequate to pay for the repairs, the developer shall pay the remaining amount. The following procedures shall apply in this situation:
(1) The city shall notify the developer in writing of such action.
(2) Upon completion of necessary maintenance repairs, the developer shall request in writing to the city for inspection of the maintenance repairs. The city shall make said inspection and in turn notify the developer of the inspection results.
(3) If the work is free from defects, and the improvements are in compliance with city specifications, the city shall provide written approval to the developer of said compliance and the maintenance bond shall be released.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 105.2, 4-24-2017)
837:
(a) The maintenance bond or letter of credit shall be for a period of 24 months. This covers the cost of maintaining the project for a period of 18 months from the date the city issues approval of the final plat or project plus six months, if needed, to complete necessary deficiencies.
(b) The maintenance bond or letter of credit shall be for a minimum of 50 percent of the total cost of the project. In its discretion the city may utilize an engineer to determine the amount of the bond or letter of credit. The bond or letter of credit shall be payable to the City of Emerson.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 105.3, 4-24-2017)
838:
(a) Upon issuance of the maintenance bond as provided above, the developer shall execute a certificate of dedication and maintenance agreement as provided by the city. All streets and rights-of-way shown upon the final plat, together with all other public improvements shall be dedicated to the city either in fee simple or by perpetual easement, as appropriate. The certificate of dedication shall be recorded by the developer in the office of the clerk of the superior court of Bartow County. The developer shall also furnish to the city an opinion by an attorney acceptable to the city that title records have been examined and that marketable fee simple title was vested in the developer at time of recording of the certificate. The city reserves the right to refuse said dedication for reasons related to construction or maintenance.
(b) The maintenance agreement shall obligate the developer, his successors and assigns to maintain the streets and improvements for a period of 18 months from date of written acceptance by the city and to correct or repair the same as required by the city. Furthermore, the developer, his successors and assigns, shall agree to hold the city harmless and indemnify the city from liabilities arising from defects in design, installation and/or maintenance during the maintenance period.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 105.4, 4-24-2017)
839:
(a) All areas containing infrastructure to be dedicated to the city or where access is required per this chapter a recordable executed easement shall be dedicated to the city. All easements shall include a plat. Easements required for a development that are off-site shall be obtained, approved and recorded before any plan approvals are issued.
(b) The city shall be provided a minimum 20-foot perpetual easement with the right to erect, construct, install, lay and thereafter use, operate, inspect, repair, maintain, replace and remove utility components and any other required equipment, together with the right of ingress and egress over the adjacent land of the development. Easements shall be a minimum of 20 feet wide, ten feet on each side of the line; except that when the depth of the utility exceeds ten feet, the required easement width shall increase such that the easement width is at least twice the depth from the ground surface to bottom of the pipe.
(c) During the period of construction, required future maintenance or reconstruction, said easement shall be enlarged to such reasonable width as to facilitate the operation, repair, or installation of equipment, after which installation, repair or reconstruction, the width of said easement shall be reduced, and the city shall, as soon as practicable, restore the condition in which said land was before construction or repair, insofar as reasonably possible, without expense to the undersigned; provided, however, the city shall not be responsible for any shrubbery, trees or other ornamentals planted or buildings, fences, sidewalks or other structures within said easement but shall only be responsible for reseeding the grass cover.
(d) The developer agrees that the easement is an exclusive agreement to the city and no other use whatsoever may be made of said easement nor shall any shrubbery, trees, plants, buildings, fences, sidewalks or other structures be placed upon said easement without the express written consent of the city. In the event any such shrubbery, trees, plants, buildings, fences, sidewalks or other structures are placed within said easement without written approval, the developer will remove the same at the developer's sole expense.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 105.5, 4-24-2017)
840:
(a) Approved as-built drawings shall be required before the final plat is recorded for subdivisions or before a certificate of occupancy is issued for commercial and industrial sites and must be the same format as the original construction plans.
(b) All as-built drawings must be on standard 24-inch by 36-inch sheets with a maximum scale of one inch equals 50 feet.
(c) "As-Built" or "Record Drawing" is to be indicated in large clear print on the plans.
(d) All plans must be in English.
(e) Electronic files must also be submitted in AutoCAD (2004 or newer), Portable Document Format (PDF) and ESRI format. Files must be geo-referenced and include all construction and project details, which truly reflect the final project as it was constructed.
(f) All datum shall be Georgia West State Plane and NAVD88 respectively.
(g) The water system as-builts shall show locations of fire hydrants, lines, valves, valve elevation, fittings, water main sizes, and types of materials.
(h) Sanitary sewer system as-builts shall show locations of manholes, lines, services, line sizes, types of materials, profiles, manhole inverts, and line grades.
(i) Street as-builts shall show street layout, profiles, and grades.
(j) Storm sewer system as-builts shall show impervious surface, locations of drainage structures and lines, line sizes and types of material, profiles and detention ponds.
(k) Commercial site layout as-builts in addition to water, sanitary sewer, and storm sewer, as-builts shall include, but not be limited to, the following final locations of buildings, entrances, parking, and grading.
(l) Casing location, material and elevation at end of pipe is required.
(m) Contour lines at two-foot intervals are required.
(n) Sprinkler system as-builts with head count are required.
(o) Road names and street/lot numbers are required.
(p) Lateral line ends must show distance from downstream manhole, depth and offset distance from the main line.
(q) Show elevations of manhole inverts and top.
(r) Show field-measured distance between manholes.
(s) For any sewer or storm lines, which are outside of paved streets, show the field-measured azimuth or bearing of the line from manhole to manhole.
(t) Show actual slope of all sewer and storm piping.
(u) Location sketch.
(v) Maximum error of as-built measurements shall be:
(1) Manhole inverts. Measure to 0.10 foot with maximum vertical error of 0.15 foot per 1,000 feet of horizontal traverse.
(2) Manhole tops. Measure to 0.10 foot with maximum vertical error of 0.50 foot per 1,000 feet of horizontal traverse.
(3) Horizontal locations. Measure to nearest one foot with allowable error of one foot per 1,000 feet of traverse.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 105.6, 4-24-2017)
841:
Before acceptance of a final plat or issuance of a conditional acceptance, the city may require various types of engineer and/or developer certifications depending on the type of development. The developer should ensure that these forms are obtained and completed prior to close out.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 105.7, 4-24-2017)
845:
The developer shall ensure that the subdivision of land meets the minimum standards set forth in the city zoning ordinance and development regulations. As well, the developer shall ensure that the proposed subdivision of land does not cause properties to become land locked.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 201, 4-24-2017)
848:
No land dedicated as a public street or other public purpose shall be opened or accepted as a public street or for any other public purpose, and no subdivision of land shall be made, nor subdivision plat, nor part thereof, shall be recorded before obtaining final approval from the city council and recorded by the clerk of the superior court of Bartow County.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 202, 4-24-2017)
851:
No person, firm, partnership, association, corporation, estate, trust, developer, subdivider or any other owner or agent shall transfer title or attempt to record the title to any land in the city, and no building permit may be issued on said land, unless:
(1) Said land existed as a single parcel of ownership, recorded as such in its entirety and present boundaries with the clerk of the superior court of Bartow County prior to the city development or zoning regulations; or
(2) Said land is shown in its entirety and present boundaries on a final plat as approved (under these or any previous applicable regulations) and duly recorded with the clerk of the superior court of Bartow County.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 203.1, 4-24-2017)
852:
No person, firm, partnership, association, corporation, estate, trust, developer, subdivider or any other owner or agent shall transfer title to any property by reference to, exhibition of, or any other use of any map of plat illustrating the subdivision of land without a final plat of said land showing said property first having been duly approved under the procedures of this chapter or any previously applicable regulations and recorded with the clerk of the superior court of Bartow County.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 203.2, 4-24-2017)
855:
(a) Minimum right-of-way. Each lot shall front upon a dedicated public street having a right-of-way of not less than 50 feet.
(b) Arrangements. Side lot lines should be at right angles (90 degrees) to straight street lines or radial to curved street lines. Side lot lines should be radial to the center points in all cul-de-sacs. Side lot lines may deviate up to five degrees if necessary to combine property corners.
(c) Building lines. Building lines shall conform to the city zoning ordinance.
(d) Double frontage lots. Access shall be restricted to the interior streets for all residential subdivisions.
(e) Minimum lot frontage. The minimum width of frontage of any lot shall be as required by the city zoning ordinance for the specific zoning district in which the lot is located. The lot width at any point from the road right-of-way to the building line shall not be less than the minimum required frontage width.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 204, 4-24-2017)
858:
All corners shall be marked with an iron pin, one-half-inch in diameter or greater and 18 inches long and driven so as to extend not less than one inch above the finished grade. If unable to penetrate ground 18 inches, then set other permanent monuments (PK nail in asphalt, spike, chiseled x, etc.).
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 205, 4-24-2017)
862:
(a) Classification of proposed streets. Prior to submission of preliminary plat, the developer shall meet with the city manager and his designee to have the proposed street classified, in order that it can be accepted into the city's system. In some cases, it may be desirable for a street to have a higher classification based upon ultimate development of the entire area, which is not necessarily just the one development being submitted. This is particularly true in the more outlying areas around the city. Street continuity may require that a cul-de-sac street be provided in a current development at the property line, such that it can be extended in the future. In a case of this nature, the current development would provide the street to the property line. The future development would pick up at the property line and continue the street.
(b) Existing streets. When development is proposed on an existing street, all improvements required under these standards shall apply to the side of the street which the development abuts.
(c) Relation to adjoining street system. The proposed street system shall extend existing streets, but to current city standards. If lots front on the existing city street, it shall be improved out to an acceptable city or county road by the developer.
(d) Alleys. Alleys may be provided to the rear of all lots except lots with double frontage.
(e) Restriction of access. When a subdivision fronts on an arterial or major collector, double frontage lots shall be provided with frontage on an interior street with no access to the arterial or major collector.
(f) Dead end streets. All dead end streets shall have a cul-de-sac as defined in the City of Emerson Standard Details.
(g) Conformity to the city street classification map. The location and width of all streets and roads shall conform as specified. Street plans and profiles shall be approved by the city.
(h) Intersections.
(1) Street intersections shall be as nearly at right angles as is possible.
(2) No intersection shall be at an angle of less than 75 degrees.
(3) The property line at street corners shall be mitered adequately to permit construction of a 13-foot clear shoulder behind the curb and gutter.
(4) Sight distance at intersections shall meet requirements of this regulation. (See City of Emerson Standard Details.)
(5) Islands at intersections shall be subject to individual approval by the city. In no case shall anything extend more than two feet above the back of the curb within the right-of-way of the street to be intersected.
(6) Landings shall be required for all intersections. These landings shall be as defined in the City of Emerson Standard Details.
(7) Opposing tee street intersections shall be directly aligned or shall be offset at least 200 feet.
(8) Intersections shall have a minimum radius as measured to the face of the curb of 40 feet for residential and commercial subdivisions and 75 feet for industrial subdivisions.
(i) Names.
(1) Proposed streets that are obviously in alignment with other already existing and named street shall bear the name of such existing street.
(2) No proposed street name shall duplicate an existing street name within the city or the county regardless of the use of the suffix "Street," "Avenue," "Boulevard," "Drive," "Place," "Way," "Court," or however otherwise designated.
(3) All street names are subject to the approval of the city.
(j) Traffic studies. The city may require that a traffic study be performed prior to the issuance of any permits to evaluate the current capacity of streets expected to carry the traffic volumes from the proposed development.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 301.1, 4-24-2017)
863:
(a) General.
(1) The minimum width of right-of-way, as measured from lot line, shall be as shown in the City of Emerson Standard Details.
(2) Adequate right-of-way shall be provided to allow the construction of a 13-foot cleared shoulder behind the curb line except industrial streets shall have a 16-foot cleared shoulder.
(3) When the development (residential or commercial) is located on only one side of an existing street, one-half of the required right-of-way as measured from the centerline of the existing right-of-way, shall be shown on the plan and is required to be dedicated to the city.
(b) Prohibitions.
(1) It shall be unlawful for any person to obstruct, encroach upon, or injure materially any part of any city right-of-way or city road pavement.
(2) No encroachments are permitted in any right-of-way of the city without permission of the city, unless otherwise permitted by this article.
(3) No building, structure, service area, or required off-street parking and loading facilities, except driveways, shall be permitted to encroach on city rights-of-way.
(4) The city shall owe no compensation for removal of illegal encroachments or obstructions.
(c) Permitted encroachments.
(1) Driveways. Driveways (including paved, masonry, asphalt, etc.) are permitted to encroach on the right-of-way. A driveway permit shall be required and the lot owner shall secure permission for any new driveway from the city. Driveways must meet sight distance requirements and must be constructed in compliance with city requirements for stormwater drainage/piping.
(2) Landscaping. Limited landscaping is permitted in the city right-of-way, including grass, flowers and shrubs not in excess of two feet in height. Trees shall not be planted in the right-of-way.
(3) Irrigation systems. Irrigation systems shall not be installed in the right-of-way.
(4) Mailbox support structures. The city permits limited encroachment of the right-of-way for mailbox support structures, which meet the following standards:
a. The use of massive mailbox support structures that, when struck, could damage vehicles and cause serious injury to vehicle occupants are prohibited. Heavy metal posts, concrete posts, brick bases, and miscellaneous items such as farm equipment or supports filled with concrete are also prohibited and cannot be used for mailbox supports.
b. Acceptable mailbox supports include:
1. A single four-inch by four-inch or four-inch diameter wooden post;
2. A metal post with strength no greater than a two-inch diameter standard strength steel hollow pipe;
3. Other support of no greater strength, as approved by the city, as in accordance with the standards of the AASHTO Roadway Design Guidelines for mailbox structures, which are incorporated herein by reference.
In the event the property owner has any question as to whether the proposed mailbox support will be permitted, the city should be consulted.
c. Mailbox supports must be embedded no more than 24 inches into the ground. A metal post shall not be fitted with an anchor plate, but it may have an anti-twist device that extends no more than ten inches below the ground surface.
d. The post-to-box attachment details should be of sufficient strength to prevent the box from separating from the post top if a vehicle strikes the installation. The mailbox itself should be of lightweight steel, wood, or plastic/composite construction, and meeting U.S. Postal Service regulations.
(d) Nonconforming encroachments.
(1) All encroachments pre-existing the date of adoption of the ordinance from which this article is derived may remain as nonconforming encroachments, unless and until removal is ordered by the city, for utility work, road work or other work necessitating access to the right-of-way. For pre-existing encroachments, the city shall give 30 days' notice of removal (unless the encroachment presents a safety hazard).
(2) Any structure pre-existing the ordinance from which this article is derived which is damaged or removed shall not be replaced in kind and must be replaced in accordance with the requirements of the ordinance from which this article is derived.
(3) The city shall owe no compensation for removal of nonconforming encroachments.
(e) Removals and notice.
(1) Right of removal. The city shall have the authority to remove without notice any encroachment or obstruction of the right-of-way. The city shall also have the authority to issue a notice of removal to property owners giving them up to 30 days to remove an unpermitted encroachment
(2) Notice of removal. Where the city determines that an encroachment must be removed from the right-of-way for construction, maintenance or safety purposes, the city may (but is not required to unless otherwise specified herein) issue a notice of removal, giving up to 30 days to remove the structure. After the deadline, the structure may be removed by the city with the costs to be charged to the property owner. The owner may also be cited, fined or have other enforcement action taken against him to secure compliance with this chapter and/or reimbursement.

915:
The design, construction, testing and approval of sanitary sewerage facilities intended to convey sewage to the City of Cartersville sewer system (Red Top Sewer), shall comply with current ordinances and regulations of the City of Cartersville, or City of Emerson, whichever are more stringent, as determined by the City of Emerson.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 401.4, 4-24-2017)
916:
All utilities shall be buried in a residential subdivision unless otherwise required by the city. This requirement may only be waived by the city; said waiver must be in writing. All utility locations shall correspond to the typical layout shown in the City of Emerson Standard Details.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 401.5, 4-24-2017)
919:
All projects, which involve construction of main sewers and/or force mains and pumping facilities, shall have detailed construction plans and specifications prepared by a registered professional engineer or licensed surveyor licensed in the state. Developments, which only involve building sewers, may have plans and specifications prepared by the project architect.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 402.1, 4-24-2017)
920:
Preliminary plans will be prepared and submitted for review as described elsewhere in the development regulations. Questions relating to availability of sewers and proposed location of connection should be resolved at this stage before proceeding with final planning. A submittal for preliminary review must include all land to be developed although the land is to be developed in several phases or units. Availability determinations will be made only for the phases of the project proposed for current construction. Availability determinations will be valid for a period of one year from the date of project approval. The developer must submit any data required for accurately projecting sewer flow quantities and rates. The developer is also responsible for furnishing any other information deemed necessary for evaluating service feasibility.
(Ord. No. 2017-005, § 402.2, 4-24-2017)
